newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends just above new contract lows.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends just above new contract lows.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures ended just above their new contract lows amid a host of bearish news, traders said.

The detection of karnal bunt fungus in Tennessee wheat and an increase in farmer-related hedging were among the chief reasons for the broadly lower price action in nearby spring wheat contracts, traders said.
Spring wheat also received pressure after the EU increased its wheat export subsidy to 19 Ecus from 13 a week ago.
A steep decline in CBOT soybean futures also contributed spillover weakness late, traders said.
"Karnal bunt got us lower. Along with that, the spread's falling apart," a MGE trader said at the midsession.
MGE spring wheat closed unchanged to 12-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with December down 12-1/2 cents at $3.85-3/4, after setting a new contract low during the seesion at $3.85.
The Dec/March spread traded at 10-1/2 cents early but narrowed throughout the session and was bid at 6-1/2 cents at the close.
Atwood-Peavey had sold 2.5 million bushels of December spring wheat, which traders linked to an increase in farmer sales. Atwood-Peavey also sold one million March.
Wilson bought one million March and three million Dec. LFG sold 1.5 million Dec and March and bought 1.5 million Dec and one million March, traders said.
MGE barley futures closed five to 10 cents per cwt lower, with Dec down 10 cents at $6.50.
